overview: Two types of electrochemical cells — one generates electricity from a spontaneous reaction, the other uses electricity to force a non-spontaneous one.
genZNote: One cell makes electricity happen. The other makes a reaction happen using electricity.

aspects.label: Energy Conversion
aspects.valueA: Chemical energy converted to electrical energy.
aspects.valueB: Electrical energy converted to chemical energy.

aspects.label: Reaction Spontaneity
aspects.valueB: Non-spontaneous redox reaction, driven forward by an external power source (ΔG positive without input).

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A battery (e.g. Daniell cell) supplying current to a circuit.
aspects.valueB: Electrolysis of molten NaCl to produce sodium metal and chlorine gas.
